courses.title: AI + Writing
courses.blurb: Two tracks on the writing that fills a working week and has your name on it - the 6-session leader track covers reading a document a model touched, the house voice written down, disclosure and over-reliance, and a one-page team standard; the 10-session writer track runs one real week at Cadence through briefs, voice capture, emails, memos, editing, difficult messages and long-form. A live classroom simulator runs 12 moments in your browser: watch the score climb 2 to 12 as the levers come on - and watch the fifth toggle, the AI detector, only ever make things worse.

A live evidence lab audits 10 claims against 7 rules, climbing 0 to 9 of 10 - and shows why adding 40 more sources costs you a claim. Fabricated-citation catching belongs to the AI + Law course; this one owns whether a real source supports the claim.

courses.title: Performance Management
courses.blurb: Grow people, and part well when you must. The craft the OKR course deliberately leaves out: ramp and the first 90 days, coaching rather than fixing (GROW, oversight matched to task-relevant maturity), growth plans people actually use, ladders translated into behaviour you can observe, and the four causes of underperformance - skill, will, fit, context - each needing a different intervention. Then the conversations nobody is taught: promotion denial, pay, "this is not working", and a managed exit with a defensible process and dignity intact. A live PIP Lab runs two meters at once: build a plan properly and recovery climbs 22% to 88% while defensibility climbs 8% to 92%, shorten it to two weeks and both collapse to 32/36, write it after the decision is made and it drops to 5/13. The case that matters most tops out at 31% recovery with a perfect 92% process, because the cause was never the person. Two tracks: 6 for CHROs and heads of function who design the system, 10 for team leads who run it. Sibling to learn-okr-with-phoebe on the same company. Not legal advice.

courses.title: OKRs & Fair Measurement
courses.blurb: How to measure people and teams fairly. A leader track (6, design the system) plus a manager track (10, run it fairly), worked on Cartwheel, an online retailer. OKRs vs KPIs, the metric tree decomposed to controllable levers, the idiosyncratic rater effect (most of a rating's variance is the rater, not the rated), bias hiding in review language, calibration that corrects instead of ranking, and AI as a bias-checking helper inside the EU AI Act / GDPR Art 22 / NYC LL144 floor. A live Fair-Metric Lab scores a metric's fairness from its real attributes, then ties it to pay and watches the number race to target while the outcome it stood for collapses. The linchpin, repeated all course: OKR scores steer and teach, they never set pay.

courses.title: Data PMO

courses.title: Classification & Regression

Sequel to intro-ml on the Lumen running case, with a live in-browser decision-boundary explorer.

courses.title: Feature Engineering
courses.blurb: A column is what the database gives you; a feature is what the model can learn from - and almost all the winnable performance lives in that gap. Two tracks: leaders learn why feature work beats model shopping, why a suspiciously good score is a red flag, and what governance costs; practitioners rebuild Lumen's checkout data through scaling, encoding, datetime, interactions, missing-data signal, selection and an honest embeddings bridge. A live workbench trains a real model in your browser - held-out AUC climbs 0.500 to 0.813 with the algorithm never changing, then the leakage lever turns 0.967 training into 0.789 held-out the moment the column that knew the future goes missing.

courses.title: Model Evaluation
courses.blurb: Every metric is an opinion about which mistakes matter. Both families in one arc: the classic canon (precision, recall, F1, ROC, calibration, cost matrices) and the LLM-era system (groundedness, hallucination, LLM-as-judge, latency and cost). A live evaluator runs in your browser: drag a real threshold on 2,000 scored sessions, press Optimize F1 and watch it cost $704 more than the money-optimal point, then calibrate an LLM judge and catch its verbosity bias red-handed. Ends with the eight-slot eval sheet you can defend line by line.

An instruction-quality simulator with five levers and a 10-task scorecard runs live on the key pages.

courses.title: Recommendation Systems
courses.blurb: How the 'recommended for you' engine works end to end - the 6-session leader track covers the families in plain English, e-commerce vs fintech logic, the team + R&R pipeline, measurement and ethics; the 10-session builder track ships real Python from basket analysis to item-item and user-user CF, content-based, matrix factorization, deep recsys, evaluation, serving and monitoring. Cites Amazon's item-to-item paper, the Netflix Prize, and Alibaba's DIN, with a real in-browser recommender you drive on the Kirana store.

courses.title: Time-Series Forecasting
courses.blurb: Predicting what a number does next, end to end - the 6-session leader track covers the shape of a series, the method ladder in plain English, the team + R&R pipeline, how a forecast is measured, and the pitfalls; the 10-session builder track ships real Python from decomposition and baselines through exponential smoothing, ARIMA/SARIMA, Prophet, gradient-boosting, and a deep-model survey, then backtesting, serving and monitoring. Follows the FPP3 canon, Box-Jenkins, and Prophet (Taylor & Letham 2018), with a real in-browser forecaster you drive on the Lumen web-analytics series.

courses.title: Anomaly Detection
courses.blurb: Finding the points that do not belong, end to end - the 6-session leader track covers the anomaly types, the method ladder in plain English, the team + R&R pipeline, why accuracy lies on rare events, and the pitfalls (alert fatigue, drift); the 10-session builder track ships real Python from statistical detectors (z-score/IQR/MAD) through rolling and seasonal, distance and density (LOF), isolation forest, one-class methods, time-series change detection, and a deep-model survey, then evaluation, serving and alerting. Cites Chandola's survey, LOF, Isolation Forest, and One-Class SVM, with a real in-browser detector you drive on the Lumen web-analytics series. Sibling to the forecasting course.

courses.title: Ecommerce Metrics
courses.blurb: Every ecommerce number, explained on one store - the 6-session leader track covers the GMV equation, the metric dictionary (visitor vs session, the two conversion rates), reading the funnel, the weekly business review, honest benchmarks by industry, and metric governance; the 8-session analyst track decomposes Mango Lane (240K visitors, 360K sessions, 9,720 orders, $660,960 GMV) completely - core four by hand, a live driver-tree simulator (edit PDP penetration or checkout completion and watch GMV move, simulate a drop and trace the coral trail), funnel gates, drop diagnosis, segment cuts and mix effects, the review pack, and the metric spec sheet. Definitions verified against GA4 and Shopify docs, benchmarked with Baymard, IRP, Dynamic Yield, and Littledata. On-ramp of the ecommerce & growth analytics series.

courses.title: User Journey Analytics
courses.blurb: Where the numbers happen: the ecommerce in-app journey, measured - the 6-session leader track reads the journey map (five entry doors and their quality, search vs browse with honestly-flagged conversion research, the PDP as decision room with Spiegel's reviews math, Baymard's checkout killers, and the reach x severity x confidence prioritization ritual); the 8-session analyst track measures it all on Mango Lane - screen map with real counts, entry-door quality and mix-vs-quality decomposition, path analysis (search 12% vs browse 4.5%), a live journey-flow simulator (toggle four classic fixes and watch conversion climb from 2.7% to 4.0%, GMV +47%), PDP engagement, the checkout micro-funnel, a full journey-leak diagnosis, and the journey scorecard. Same store and month as the metrics course - every count reconciles to the order. Course 2 of the ecommerce & growth analytics series.

courses.title: AI Agents
courses.blurb: What an agent actually is - an LLM in a loop with tools - and how to make one reliable. Two tracks: leaders learn workflows-vs-agents, the seven guardrail types and when NOT to build; builders assemble the Daybreak Ops Agent in raw Python across tools, memory, planning, guardrails and evals. A live agent simulator runs the 12-task golden set in your browser: watch the score climb 1 to 12 as you switch the four levers on, catch a real prompt injection, and gate an irreversible send behind draft-and-hold.

courses.title: AI Infrastructure
courses.blurb: The platform behind your whole data team, as eight layers and five personas. Leaders get the investment case: where the money actually goes, why every published GPU TCO analysis concludes rent and who wrote them, and what really happened in the platform builds that published numbers. Practitioners build the reference architecture layer by layer - storage economics, the catalog as the real lock-in surface, orchestration, lakehouse, semantic layer, MLOps, LLM gateway - with honest cost bands and named options throughout. A live simulator computes the monthly bill from published rate cards as your five people come unblocked, then shows what analytics egress costs and why self-serve bought before a semantic layer produces confident wrong answers.

courses.title: Agent Launch Gate
courses.blurb: Given all the eval numbers, do you ship? The launch-gate capstone over the eval courses: pick criteria per bot archetype, size a golden set until it proves something, and run a six-gate scorecard where quality cannot buy off cost. Three archetypes gated end to end - a support chatbot with no ground truth, a text-to-query bot whose answers are executable, and an analytics bot where errors compound. A live gate computes a real 95% Wilson interval in your browser: watch confidence climb from 76.4%, the honest reading of a nineteen-out-of-twenty demo, to 92.5% where it can be signed - and twice along the way nothing about the bot changes at all.

courses.title: AI Observability
courses.blurb: Evals tell you whether it works; this tells you what actually happened. Tuesday 09:14, an analytics bot starts sending executives stale numbers - no error, no alert, green dashboard - because two thirds of the run sits inside no span at all. Spans and the current OpenTelemetry GenAI conventions including the names that changed under you, instrumenting an agent loop that is width rather than depth, per-span cost and latency, the empirical failure taxonomy, tail sampling, burn-rate alerting, and the privacy split that keeps you debuggable and compliant. A live trace explorer computes real arithmetic in your browser: switch coverage on one lever at a time and watch the visible wall clock climb 32.4% to 100% while the diagnosis goes zero of five questions to five - then switch on full prompt capture and watch the diagnosis refuse to move while retention jumps ten and a half times.

courses.title: AI Red Team
courses.blurb: Testing the AI systems you own, honestly, and what you may claim afterwards. A bug bounty ran 183 people over 3,000 hours and found no universal jailbreak; a later exercise with 339 people found one - red teaming establishes presence, never absence. Defensive throughout: attack classes named so you can build test cases, each paired with its defence, no exploit payloads. Scoping and rules of engagement, the OWASP 2026 and MITRE ATLAS taxonomies, injection, refusal, extraction and tool abuse, then build the suite and harden. A live attack-surface board counts an untested class at FULL risk, so it reports unknown rather than safe: probe the whole surface and the total moves only 99.3 to 96.4 while unknown risk goes 86% to zero. The system-prompt guard everyone reaches for first removes 3.6 points; least-privilege plus human approval removes 55.
